original.reason: Lemma 1 is not proved: earlier terms need not occupy distinct residue classes modulo n, so the stated counting argument is false. Also, increments of m_n by at most one do not imply m_n-n tends to -infinity; an additional argument is required.

judgment.reason: The derivation of the two-choice recurrence omits the necessary bound m_{n-1}<n; without it, m_{n-1}-n may be a positive smaller congruent candidate. Further, m_n increasing by at most one does not imply m_n-n tends to -infinity.
The two-choice claim is unsupported without proving m_{n-1}<n, and the asserted limit m_n-n to -infinity does not follow merely from unit-sized possible increases.
It omits the required bound excluding positive lower congruent candidates in establishing the recurrence, and its conclusion that m_n-n tends to -infinity from increment size alone is invalid.

The simultaneous induction does not establish the needed m_{n-1}<n bound before claiming only one positive smaller congruent candidate. It also incorrectly infers m_n-n tends to -infinity from m_n increasing by at most one.
